title: Pluggable stream proxy for TypeScript SDK: unified async-iterable/WebStream with progress checkpoints and resume tokens
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description:
Problem: The TypeScript SDK currently exposes both AsyncIterable<T> and ReadableStream/WHATWG streams but lacks a composable abstraction to: (1) insert progress checkpoints into a stream, (2) generate small resume tokens for partial consumption, and (3) swap implementations (AsyncIterable <-> Web Stream) without duplicating consumer code. This causes friction for clients who want robust retry/resume semantics and telemetry (e.g., per-chunk latency, token cost) across different runtimes (Node/Deno/Browser).

Goals:
- Provide a lightweight, pluggable proxy layer that can wrap any stream-like source (AsyncIterable<Uint8Array | string>, ReadableStream) and export both AsyncIterable and ReadableStream views.
- Allow insertion of checkpoint hooks that emit checkpoint metadata (byte offsets, token counts, chunk checksums) to a monitoring sink or to produce resumable tokens.
- Offer a standard resume-token format (opaque, small) that encodes the minimal state required to resume from the last checkpoint.
- Ensure minimal overhead: target <1% p99 token latency increase and <3% CPU overhead in typical workloads.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement server-side continuation support; it assumes the backend can accept a resume token as a request header and replay from a partial prefix.
- Not implementing a full-on persistence/store for checkpoints - checkpoints are emitted to a pluggable sink (in-memory, metrics, optional local store) and the SDK consumer is responsible for storing tokens when needed.

Design summary:
- Core primitive: PluggableStreamProxy<T> constructed with a source and optional plugins. Plugins include CheckpointPlugin, RetryFencePlugin, and FramingPlugin.
- Public API: proxy.asAsyncIterable(), proxy.asReadableStream(), and proxy.currentResumeToken().
- Checkpoints are produced at configurable intervals (by bytes, by logical chunk, or by token-budget heuristic). Each checkpoint includes: sequenceId, byteOffset, lastChunkHash, and timestamp. The resume token is base64(signed-json) to keep it compact and opaque.

Example usage (TypeScript):

const source = client.streamText({ model: 'redwood-compact' }); // returns AsyncIterable<string> (example)
const proxy = new PluggableStreamProxy(source, {
  plugins: [
    new CheckpointPlugin({ bytesInterval: 8192 }),
    new RetryFencePlugin({ maxRetries: 3 })
  ]
});

// Consume as async iterable (Node/Deno consumers)
for await (const chunk of proxy.asAsyncIterable()) {
  // process chunk
  // periodically call proxy.currentResumeToken() to persist checkpoint
}
// Or consume as Web ReadableStream (Browser consumers)
const rs = proxy.asReadableStream();
const reader = rs.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  // process value
}
// If a network error occurs, consumer can pass the last persisted token back into client.streamText to resume.

Plugin notes:
- CheckpointPlugin: configurable by bytes, chunks, or heuristics; emits checkpoint objects via an async callback or metrics hook. Optionally signs tokens with SDK-managed key to prevent tampering.
- RetryFencePlugin: ensures that when we reconnect and resume using a token, client-side duplicate chunks are eliminated by fencing on sequenceId. Works with server-side idempotency keys if available.
- FramingPlugin: handles framing boundaries (e.g., newline-delimited JSON, SSE, protobuf frames) and ensures checkpoints are aligned to frame boundaries where requested.

Observability:
- Proxy emits events (checkpoint, chunk-metrics, resume-attempt, resume-success, resume-failure) to the SDK event bus. These map to Console traces and are optionally forwarded to user telemetry via a sink.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for proxy conversion paths (async->readable and readable->async) with synthetic sources that inject errors at various positions.
- Integration test that mocks backend resume behavior: produce a stream, simulate mid-stream disconnect, resume with token and verify no data duplication and correct continuation.
- Benchmark harness against current streaming path for small/medium/long sequences; target under 1% p95 latency regression.
- Fuzz tests for resume token corruption and plugin exception handling.

Compatibility and migration:
- Default behavior is backward-compatible: if no plugins passed, PluggableStreamProxy acts as a thin identity adapter (zero-copy where possible).
- SDK exports a helper: tsSDK.wrapStreamWithProxy(source, options) to encourage gradual adoption in existing SH client code.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (alpha): enable for internal Redwood feature flags; instrument two internal customers (console telemetry ingestion, dedicated agent log streaming).
- Phase 2 (beta): expose to public SDK with docs + examples; opt-in by default.
- Phase 3 (GA): document resume semantics in API docs and enable for a managed resume header path if backend support lands.

Implementation risk and trade-offs:
- State size: checkpoint frequency trades off token size vs recovery granularity. Recommend conservative default (8KB) and guidance in docs.
- Security: if resume tokens include offsets and hashes, consider signing to avoid replay attacks across tenants. We will not ship signing on GA until KMS integration is available; initial signing will use ephemeral SDK key.

Open questions (to resolve in design review):
1) Canonical resume token format: JSON vs binary protobuf? (JSON base64 chosen for early compatibility).
2) Default checkpoint interval: 8KB vs 4KB? (benchmarks will decide).
3) Whether server should provide a short-lived continuation nonce to tighten security.

comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Rodriguez: Triage - flagged as P1 due to developer ergonomics complaints from DDS team. Related to many prior streaming interop tickets; suggested a plugin-based approach rather than a monolithic adapter.

2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Spike completed - created a small prototype that wraps AsyncIterable and exposes a ReadableStream in ~120 lines of TS. Performance looks promising on local workloads. See prototype PR for code.

2026-03-06 - PM review (Riley Park): Product requested explicit API examples for resume UX (how callers persist and reuse tokens). Added example and clarified that SDK won't auto-persist tokens by default.
2026-03-09 - Design review (Maya Singh): Suggested adding FramingPlugin to avoid checkpointing mid-json-object for many customers. Added to design notes.

2026-03-12 - Security (Jordan Patel): Raised concern about token replay across tenants; recommended plan to sign tokens. Marked security_review_required=false for this ticket but requested follow-up for KMS integration before GA.
2026-03-14 - Liam Chen: Implemented checkpoint event and currentResumeToken() surface. Running integration tests against mocked backend resume endpoint. Next: benchmarks and docs.
next_steps: Finish integration tests, run benchmark suite, address token signing plan with security team, prepare RFC for public docs and examples, and schedule canary with internal consumers.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on client-side ergonomics and observability. Server-side resume semantics will be captured in a follow-up ticket after we validate token shape with backend teams.
